verdict: BXP rent revenue rose 5% to $911M and total occupancy climbed to 89.4%, swinging the office landlord back to a $114M GAAP profit — helped by gains on building sales — while its headline FFO was $302M.

kpis.label: FFO (non-GAAP)
kpis.note: $1.89 per diluted share — the REIT headline measure

kpis.label: Total occupancy
kpis.note: up 100 basis points from Q2, a fourth straight gain

segments.name: Lease revenue
segments.note: Rent from premier office buildings in Boston, New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle and Washington, DC — 93% of all revenue.

segments.name: Hotel
segments.note: Revenue from the company's hotel property — about flat.

segments.name: Development & management services
segments.note: Fees for developing and managing buildings for others.

segments.name: Payroll reimbursements
segments.note: Payroll costs billed straight back under management contracts — money in and straight back out (see the matching cost line).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Non-cash charge spreading the cost of buildings over their lives — the biggest single expense, and the one FFO adds back.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — includes $0.1M of transaction costs.

opex.name: Payroll for management contracts
opex.note: Staff costs that are reimbursed dollar-for-dollar by clients (see revenue).

takeaways.title: Occupancy keeps climbing
takeaways.text: Total portfolio occupancy rose 100 basis points to 89.4% — a fourth straight quarterly gain — and the CBD portfolio was 91.8% occupied. BXP signed 74 leases for about 1.2M square feet at a 10.3-year average term.

takeaways.title: FFO is the number REIT readers watch
takeaways.text: Funds from Operations (non-GAAP) were $302M, or $1.89 per diluted share, up from $1.74 a year ago. FFO adds back building depreciation, which is why it sits well above GAAP EPS of $0.71.

takeaways.title: Building sales flattered GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Selling Sumner Square and 1330 Connecticut Avenue in Washington, DC for about $155M produced about $10M of gains. Management raised full-year guidance to EPS of $2.35–$2.37 and FFO of $7.06–$7.08 per share.

oneTimers: Gains on sales of real estate of $10M in the quarter (about $10.5M on the two Washington, DC sales, per the release) — included in GAAP profit above and excluded from FFO.
Headline non-GAAP measure: FFO of $302M ($1.89 per diluted share). This page is built on the GAAP income statement; FFO adds back $229M of depreciation and amortization and removes the sales gains.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $159M, partly offset by $10M of gains on real estate sales, $8M of interest and other income and $1M from joint ventures, less $1M of securities losses — a net $140M cost after rounding.
footerNote: Cost of revenue here is the direct cost of running the properties: rental operating expenses of $335M plus hotel operating expenses of $10M. The flow uses total net income of $155M; after $41M attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to BXP, Inc. was $114M ($0.71 per diluted share).
